title: Review of c11's active-nematic res15 finding: at 1.5x resolution seed 13 grows a colony from one founder (7 persistent splits, generation 3), seed 12 nucleates nothing; founding is rare on the fine grid
summary: Two fresh seeds of the unchanged colony world at dx=2/3, 192^2 (WORLD_P dx=0.6667), T=1000. Seed 13: one droplet nucleates at t~85, orders into a rod with a vortex pair by t=220, then elongates, pinches at the middle and divides; its line grows into 10 rods by t=1000 (labkit: 10 splits, 7 persistent, max generation 3, 2 merges, 1 nucleation) with rods of the same shape as at dx=1, as the finding states. Seed 12: faint nuclei appear and dissolve by t~220 and the field stays uniform to t=1000 (0 components). The per-pixel noise amplitude is kept fixed when the grid is refined, so the initial noise per unit area is weaker at dx=2/3, which plausibly explains why founding is rarer; once a founder exists, fission is resolution-robust.

observations.D: rerun_res15/seed13/lineage.png: 7 persistent splits, max generation 3, merge/split 0.2 at dx=2/3; sheet t=220-1000 shows elongate-and-pinch fissions of rods

seeds_run.result: pass: one founder, 10 rods by t=1000
no founder nucleates; uniform from t~220

verdicts.limitation: Founding at 1.5x resolution is a rare event (1 founder on seed 13, 0 on seed 12, 1 on the author's seed 0), so S at the fine grid rests on single nucleations; the noise is per pixel, not per area. Motility at dx=2/3 is short (max 2.6 body lengths on seed 13).
